checked_non_problem_annotations.claim: Invariant support gives the correct geometric alternative
hypotheses: mu is a geodesic-flow invariant probability measure on the compact cosphere bundle.
F=supp(mu) contains no S*Sigma of the stated type.
Theorem3.3 is taken as the orbit-closure input.
result: A measure-preserving homeomorphism preserves support, so U=S*M minus F is open and geodesic-invariant.
If U missed one full V+ orbit, its closed invariant complement would contain the joint geodesic/V+ orbit closure.
Theorem3.3 identifies that closure with S*Sigma, contradicting the assumption. The same argument applies to V-.
Thus U meets every complete fast orbit of both signs. This is an orbit-intersection property; topological density alone is insufficient.
checked_non_problem_annotations.counterchecks: Both invariance and closedness of the complement are used. A nonempty arbitrary observation set does not meet the theorem hypotheses.

checked_non_problem_annotations.claim: A single h-independent cutoff can observe both fast flows
result: Lemma3.1(1) separately yields compact K+ and K- inside U meeting all orbits of their respective flows.
K=K+ union K- is compact, contained in U, and meets all V± orbits.
Choose a fixed smooth symbol a equal to1 near K, with compact support in an annular neighborhood of S*M whose intersection with S*M lies in U.
This a belongs to S^0_(1,0), is independent of h, and has a nonzero set meeting both orbit families. The control constant therefore stays fixed along the sequence.
checked_non_problem_annotations.counterchecks: Compactness is used to get the compact orbit-hitting sets. An h-dependent choice could invalidate fixed constants and is not substituted.

checked_non_problem_annotations.claim: The cutoff norm vanishes in the semiclassical limit
result: The image of (4.4) confirms Op_h(a)*=Op_h(conjugate(a))+O(h). Together with (4.1), this gives Op_h(a)*Op_h(a)=Op_h(|a|²)+O(h) in L² operator norm.
Because ||u_j||=1, the expectation of the operator remainder is O(h_j).
The fixed compact smooth symbol |a|² is an admissible test in (1.3), so ||Op_hj(a)u_j||² tends to integral |a|² dmu.
mu is supported on S*M and supp(a) is disjoint from supp(mu) there, hence that integral is0.
checked_non_problem_annotations.counterchecks: The conjugate bar is necessary. Expectation convergence for a alone would not imply norm convergence; the |a|² product/adjoint identity supplies it.

checked_non_problem_annotations.claim: Exact eigenfunctions produce the contradiction in Theorem1.3
result: h_j=lambda_j^{-1} tends to0, and smooth eigenfunctions lie in H²(M).
(-h_j² Delta_g-I)u_j=0, so the entire C log(1/h_j)/h_j residual term in (4.24) vanishes.
The fixed-symbol control estimate therefore yields1<=C||Op_hj(a)u_j|| for all sufficiently large j.
This contradicts the norm limit0 and establishes the implication conditional on Theorems3.3 and4.3.
checked_non_problem_annotations.counterchecks: For a quasimode the residual would need its own smallness after multiplication by log(1/h)/h. No additional quasimode theorem is claimed.

result: If q lies in supp(mu), the inverse image of every neighborhood of pi(q) is an open neighborhood of q with positive mu measure.
Hence pi(supp(mu)) is contained in supp(pi_*mu). Projecting S*Sigma gives Sigma as an image, so Theorem1.2 follows.
The argument does not require an injective immersion. If no proper admissible Sigma exists, the theorem's allowed submanifold has image M, giving full support.
checked_non_problem_annotations.counterchecks: Inclusion of a lower-dimensional cosphere bundle in support does not imply it carries positive mu mass, nor that support equals that cosphere bundle.

checked_non_problem_annotations.claim: Complex dimension-one boundary, conditional geometric interpretation
result: A positive-dimensional complex immersion into a connected complex curve has the same dimension as its target and is locally a diffeomorphism.
Its image is open; a compact domain has compact, hence closed, image in the Hausdorff target.
The nonempty image is therefore all of M. Thus the support conclusion, if applied in complex dimension one, has no proper-submanifold alternative.
checked_non_problem_annotations.counterchecks: This is an elementary consequence of the submanifold hypotheses, not a new verification of the surface result or of every formula in the higher-dimensional geometric setup for n=1.
